title: AS2 compiler: switch uses ActionEquals2 (0x49) instead of ActionStrictEquals (0x66)
description:
In compiler.ts compileSwitchStmt(), line 1063 emits 0x49 (ActionEquals2, abstract == equality) for case comparisons. JavaScript switch uses === (strict equality), which is ActionStrictEquals (0x66).

The comment on that line even says 'ActionEquals2 — strict equality' which is self-contradicting — 0x49 is abstract equality, not strict equality.

Impact: switch(x) { case 1: ... } will match when x is '1' (a string), '1.0', true (for case 1), or 1 (number) due to type coercion. For example, switch('1') { case 1: ... } would match case 1, which should NOT match under strict equality semantics.

Fix: change line 1063 from this.emit(0x49) to this.emit(0x66) (ActionStrictEquals). Also update all three test files (switch.test.ts, switchstmt.test.ts, switchcase.test.ts) that assert 0x49 is present — they should assert 0x66 instead.

Verified: ActionEquals2 = 0x49 and ActionStrictEquals = 0x66 confirmed against ruffle/swf/src/avm1/opcode.rs. The binary expression compiler already correctly uses 0x49 for == and 0x66 for ===.
